contracts.description: The City of Doncaster Council (CDC) is seeking to commission a Supported Accommodation and Floating Support service for young children, young people and families or parents to be.  The successful provider should provide a safe, supportive environment and be committed to providing a sensitive, non-judgemental, and non-oppressive service. The provider will need to clearly demonstrate a commitment to multi-agency working and provide a holistic approach to ensure successful outcomes are achieved and sustained by the family.  The supported accommodation provision for the young person is intended to be of a short-term duration (maximum of 12 months) for young parent/s over 16 years of age up to 25 years of age. It is the intention that individuals will move on where appropriate in a planned manner. To this end the provider will develop the children, young people, and family's ability to live independently. The provision will deliver a programme of support. The level of support offered will vary and will be based on the ongoing assessed needs of each family. Needs will be assessed through the completion of either a early help assessment or social care assessment.   The supported accommodation aspect of the service will consist of a core building and dispersed property consisting of a minimum of 13 two-bedroom properties located within the City of Doncaster area (to be sourced by The Provider)  The floating support aspect of the Service will provide support for a minimum of 65 families at any one time (for a maximum of 12 months in respect of each family). This includes a whole family approach support package, for those who are either leaving the supported accommodation and require ongoing support to set up and maintain their tenancy as well as those who are already living in other arrangements

contracts.title: Big Picture Learning - Social Impact Bond
contracts.description:
Doncaster has been identified by the DfE as a social mobility cold spot. It is among the bottom 3 LAs in the county for both persistent absence and fixed term exclusion.

Working with the Innovation Unit the council has pre-secured funding from the Life Chance Fund and a social investor to contribute towards the delivery of new educational service under a Social Impact Bond (SIB) as the vehicle to fund and improve Educational Outcomes relating to children within Doncaster. The resulting contract will be with A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) that will be set up by the successful economic operator.

Doncaster has awarded a project to address poor engagement and progress within education amongst a cohort of 11-16 year olds in Doncaster identified as having low social mobility. Over a 6 year period, it will work with approximately 204 students from across the borough through an innovative educational model called Big Picture Learning. Built around their passions and interests it will unlock engagement (demonstrated by attendance), progression in learning and increased resilience.

For some young people it will provide an alternative to the Pupil Referral Unit, for others, it will mean more specialist support than they are currently receiving in mainstream school. It will help to ensure that education providers and commissioners are better able to match the needs of pupils to the placement that they enter.

The innovative solution provided by the successful provider will help engage children back into education.

The values set out are indicative only and will depend on, performance and the final number of students who progress through the scheme.

contracts.title: Commissioned Care and Support at Home
contracts.description:
Doncaster Metropolitan Borough Council and NHS Doncaster Clinical Commissioning Group invite detailed proposals from experienced Providers to deliver a new care and support service in Doncaster, known as Commissioned Care and Support at Home.  

The Contract will commence on Monday 3rd October 2016 and will run for a period of 7 years with the opportunity to extend for a further 3 years (1 X 2 years and 1 X 1 year).

The new service will deliver support to Individuals with varying assessed levels of needs, in order for them to live at home and within their community for as long as it is safe and appropriate to do so. In all cases, the focus is on helping people to optimise their independence through the provision of personal care, support with daily living, essential domestic tasks and the promotion of wellbeing.   The focus is on achieving the agreed outcomes, as defined by the Individual. Person centred planning is robustly embedded and puts the Individual and their Carers at the forefront of all decision making.

The contract opportunity has been split into seven (7) Lots as follows:
	Lots 1 to 6 - Strategic Lead Providers 
The Borough will be split into 6 geographical areas, with Strategic Lead Providers able to bid for up to two areas (a minimum of 4 Strategic Lead Providers are required to operate within the borough). 
	Lot 7 - Additional Support Providers.
Contracts shall be awarded to tenderers that pass the selection process and achieve the minimum quality score of 60% and will have the opportunity to deliver services borough wide.

Tenderers should note a tender information event to provide information on the procurement process will take place on the 9th of June 2016. There will be two sessions, one in the morning and an identical session in the afternoon. A lunch will be provided for all attendees to act as a cross over between sessions. 

The sessions are as follows:

10:30 - 12:00 AM session

12:00 - 13:00 Lunch

13:00 - 14:30 PM
